page: The Vultr vcg-a16-6c-60g-16vram is a dedicated metal instance built for compute environments requiring dedicated hardware acceleration alongside substantial memory capacity. The platform is driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, configured with 6 dedicated vCPUs over 3 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The system includes 60 GB of main system memory, translating to an allocation of 10 GB per core. Accelerator hardware consists of a single NVIDIA A16 GPU from the Ampere architecture family, offering 16 GB of GDDR6 VRAM. High-speed local storage is bundled directly via a 350 GB NVMe SSD, and each instance provides one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations place the CPU and memory subsystems predominantly within the middle tier for mid-range instances. In synthetic compute benchmarks, the server achieved a single-core Geekbench score of 1423 and a multi-core score of 6248, complemented by a PassMark CPU score of 10812.15. CPU instruction support includes AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, assisting vector calculations and compilation tasks. However, memory-intensive and parallel decompression metrics show performance limitations, with PassMark memory and database operation scores falling into the lower quartile. In machine learning tests, the A16 GPU processes lightweight models reliably, sustaining 128.99 tokens per second on a 135M parameter text generation model, but drops to 4.78 tokens per second when scaled to a 7B parameter model.

The instance delivers qualitative cost efficiency for targeted workloads that need hardware video encoding, virtual desktop infrastructure, or lightweight inference without the expense of enterprise training accelerators. The NVIDIA A16 is tailored for high-density video streaming, remote workstation graphics, and computer vision tasks. Coupled with 60 GB of system memory and fast local NVMe storage, the vcg-a16-6c-60g-16vram is best suited for media encoding pipelines, small-scale AI model serving, graphical rendering, and memory-heavy web services.
